name: Differentiated Capabilities

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests which product or company capabilities are meaningfully distinct from real customer alternatives.
positioning.productLabel: Differentiated-Capability Lens — based on April Dunford's public positioning method

attribution.display: Based on April Dunford's public positioning method

neutralParaphrase: Compare current, usable capabilities with the real alternatives identified from customer evidence. Retain only differences that are true, relevant to the scoped offering, and available in the buying context; separate roadmap, implementation service, brand, and table-stakes claims.

locator.value: Five components; differentiated features/capabilities after alternatives
03:14-13:31, alternatives, capabilities, outcomes, and value concepts
Official book learning outcomes: five component pieces and unique value

requiredConditions: OA2-02 has produced a customer-grounded alternative set.
The capability exists now or is clearly labeled future.
Product proof can be compared at equivalent scope and conditions.

requiredEvidence.description: Current capability compared with each major alternative, including prerequisites, limits, and parity.
Best-fit customers actually use or depend on the claimed capability.
GA/beta/roadmap status, configuration, services, integration, data, and contract requirements.

decisionQuestions: Is the capability available and usable in the target customer's context?
Do best-fit customers use it in a way alternatives cannot match?
Is the difference durable, temporary, or merely implementation effort?
positiveSignals: A current capability is demonstrably absent or weaker in relevant alternatives.
Best-fit users depend on the difference in real workflows.
Prerequisites and service requirements are transparent.
The company distinguishes table stakes, parity, and true differences.
redFlags: Roadmap or demo-only capability is presented as current.
The distinction disappears after configuration, services, or pricing are normalized.
disconfirmingEvidence: A named competitor matches the capability in current production.
Customers achieve the same outcome through a manual or adjacent tool.
Usage is low among purported best-fit customers.
The capability is differentiated but easy to copy and not strategically important.
contraindications: Do not compare features without the OA2-02 alternative set.
Do not merge future roadmap with current capability.
Do not infer value from novelty.

instructions: Separate parity, difference, roadmap, and service effort.
Conclude differentiated, conditionally differentiated, parity, or insufficient.

sourceReliability.medium: Product proof and some customer use.
sourceReliability.high: Technical proof, telemetry, customers, and alternative verification converge.

evidenceStrength.high: Repeated, decision-relevant difference in best-fit workflows.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Major alternatives and usage partly covered.
evidenceCoverage.high: All major alternatives, availability, prerequisites, use, parity, and roadmap covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Purchase context depends on specific capability differences.

empiricalQualifications: Product usage and differentiation are segment-specific.

rights.notes: Public author method is neutrally paraphrased.

openIssues: Define proof levels for capability and competitor parity.
